---
title: "Perihilar Cholangiocarcinoma: Presurgical Management"
format:
  revealjs:
    theme: dark
---

## Overview {.smaller}

- **Incidence**: 1–2 per 100,000 in Western countries (lower than Asia)
- **Definition (AJCC)**: Distal to 2nd-order intrahepatic ducts, proximal to cystic duct insertion
- **Resectability**: Only ~1/3 of patients
- **5-year OS after resection**: Up to 35%
- **90-day mortality**: 5–18% (West), 1–3% (East)
- **Key principle**: Refer to expert center **before** any biliary intervention

::: {.callout}
**Critical**: High-quality imaging must be obtained **before** biliary stenting
:::

---


## Clinical Presentation {.smaller}

| Feature | Frequency |
|---------|-----------|
| Painless jaundice | ~90% |
| Cholangitis | ~10% |
| Anorexia | ~50% |
| Fatigue | ~50% |
| Weight loss / Sarcopenia | ~50% |

- Physical exam: Palpable mass in upper abdomen → unilateral lobar hypertrophy with contralateral atrophy
- Rarely presents without jaundice (isolated left/right hepatic duct involvement)

---

## Laboratory Workup {.smaller}

- **Cholestatic pattern** on liver function tests
- **CA 19-9**: Elevated in most patients
  - May be falsely elevated due to biliary obstruction
  - ~10% of patients do not produce CA 19-9 (Lewis antigen negative)
- **IgG4**: Helps diagnose autoimmune cholangitis
  - 4-fold increase nearly excludes pCCA
  - **HISORt criteria**: Histology, Imaging, Serology, Other organ involvement, Response to steroids
- **Liver fluke serology**: In endemic areas (*Clonorchis*, *Opisthorchis*)

---

## Imaging Strategy {.smaller}

| Modality | Role | Accuracy |
|----------|------|----------|
| **CT (multiphase, thin-slice)** | Arterial/portal involvement, staging | Arterial: 93%, Portal: 87% |
| **MRI + MRCP** | Biliary extent, discriminate benign causes | Superior to CT for biliary tree |
| **PET-CT** | Staging | Specificity only 67% (inflammation causes false positives) |

::: {.callout}
**Important limitation**: Lymph node sensitivity poor (54%); biliary extent often underestimated on CT
:::

- **MRI/MRCP superior** for: Mirizzi syndrome, intrahepatic lithiasis, PSC
- **Imaging after stenting is impaired** — refer before drainage!

---

## Tissue Diagnosis {.smaller}

- **Brush cytology sensitivity**: <40%
- **FISH (fluorescent in situ hybridization)** for polysomy:
  - Doubles sensitivity when added to cytology
  - Only significant predictor of malignancy in PSC patients with dominant stricture
  - CA 19-9 ≥129 + polysomy → HR 11
- **Percutaneous biopsy**: **Avoid** if transplant candidate (needle track metastases)
- **Suspicious lymph nodes**: EUS-FNA or resection at staging laparoscopy

---

## Expert Consensus (AHPBA / NCCN / ENS-CCA) {.smaller}


- Minimum workup: LFTs, CA 19-9, high-quality cross-sectional imaging (chest/abdomen/pelvis), cholangiography — **preferably before stenting**
- Early multidisciplinary consultation with expert surgeon
- **Pathologic confirmation NOT required** before surgical exploration if benign etiologies excluded and staging complete
- **No percutaneous/laparoscopic biopsy** if transplant candidate
- PET-CT **not** recommended as routine staging tool


---

# Classification and Staging

## Bismuth-Corlette Classification {.smaller}

Based solely on **biliary tree involvement**:

- **Type I**: Common hepatic duct
- **Type II**: Bifurcation (reaches confluence)
- **Type IIIa**: Extends into right hepatic duct
- **Type IIIb**: Extends into left hepatic duct
- **Type IV**: Multifocal or bilateral extension to 2nd-order ducts

::: {.callout}
**Limitation**: Does NOT account for radial extent (vascular involvement, liver invasion, atrophy)
:::

---

## MSKCC / Blumgart Staging {.smaller}

Incorporates **vascular involvement** and **lobar atrophy**:

| Stage | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| **T1** | Bile duct bifurcation ± unilateral extension to 2nd-order ducts |
| **T2** | Unilateral vascular involvement **OR** unilateral lobar atrophy |
| **T3** | Bilateral/contralateral 2nd-order duct involvement, bilateral vascular involvement, or contralateral atrophy |

::: {.callout}
Both Bismuth and MSKCC perform **poorly** in predicting resectability (~50% of explored patients are unresectable)
:::

---

## AJCC/UICC TNM (8th Edition)

- T-stage relies heavily on **vascular invasion** (portal vein or hepatic artery, unilateral or bilateral)
- Does not define how vascular invasion is determined on imaging
- Does not define what extent is still resectable
- **Prognostic accuracy**: Slightly improved vs 7th edition for resected patients, but remains poor for unresectable disease

---

# Preoperative Considerations

## Resectability Goals

1. **Margin-negative (R0) resection**
2. **Adequate Future Liver Remnant (FLR)**

- Typically requires **hemihepatectomy or greater** + en bloc caudate resection + extrahepatic bile duct resection + lymphadenectomy
- Complex biliary reconstruction (often multiple hepaticojejunostomies)
- Sometimes requires portal vein reconstruction

---

## Determining Resection Side {.smaller}

| Factor | Determines |
|--------|------------|
| Unilateral lobar atrophy | Resect atrophic side |
| Unilateral 2nd-order duct involvement | Resect involved side |
| Unilateral portal vein involvement | Resect involved side |
| Unilateral hepatic artery involvement | Resect involved side |

- **Bismuth I or II without atrophy/vascular involvement**: Either side possible
- **Left-sided resection preferred when possible**:
  - Left lateral sector <20% in 80% of patients
  - Left hemiliver <20% in 10% of patients
  - Right liver larger → higher risk of postoperative morbidity/liver failure

---

## FLR Requirements

- **Minimum FLR**: ≥25% of total liver volume (normal liver, no chemotherapy, no biliary obstruction)
- **pCCA patients**: Typically need **>30–40%** due to biliary obstruction
- Must include ≥2 contiguous segments with intact:
  - Arterial inflow
  - Portal venous inflow
  - Portal venous outflow

---

## Risk Factors for Postoperative Mortality {.smaller}

**Risk Score Model** (Wiggers et al.):

| Risk Factor | OR | 95% CI | P |
|-------------|-----|--------|---|
| Age (per 10 years) | 2.1 | 1.4–3.3 | .001 |
| Preoperative cholangitis | 4.1 | 1.8–9.4 | .001 |
| Incomplete drainage + FLR <50% | 2.8 | 1.1–7.5 | .04 |
| FLR <30% | 2.9 | 1.2–6.9 | .02 |
| Portal vein reconstruction | 2.3 | 0.9–5.8 | .09 |

**Predicted 90-day mortality**:

- Low risk (0–2 points): **2%**
- Intermediate (3–4 points): **11%**
- High risk (5–9 points): **37%**

---

## Additional Risk Factors for Liver Failure

- Albumin <3.5 g/dL
- Preoperative total bilirubin >3 mg/dL (51 μmol/L)
- Preoperative cholangitis
- FLR <30%

::: {.callout}
**Age is the most important poor prognostic factor** — risk increases rapidly with advanced age
:::

---

# Optimizing the Future Liver Remnant

## Indications for Biliary Drainage


- Cholangitis
- Jaundice + planned neoadjuvant therapy
- Liver or renal insufficiency possibly related to hyperbilirubinemia
- **Small FLR (<50%), especially before portal vein embolization**


::: {.callout}
**Target bilirubin**: <2 mg/dL (34 μmol/L) before surgery
:::

---

## Biliary Drainage Techniques {.smaller}

| Technique | Notes |
|-----------|-------|
| **EBD** (Endoscopic) | Higher crossover rate (56%), more procedures needed |
| **PTBD** (Percutaneous) | Higher technical success (93% vs 74%), but RCT showed higher 90-day mortality (41% vs 11%) |
| **ENBD** (Nasobiliary) | Japanese guidelines recommendation; less cholangitis than EBD |

---

## RCT: EBD vs PTBD {.smaller}

**Multicenter RCT** (4 expert centers, n=54, interim analysis):

| Outcome | PTBD | EBD |
|---------|------|-----|
| 90-day mortality | **41%** | **11%** (RR 3.67, P=.03) |
| Technical success | 93% | 74% |
| Therapeutic success (1 week) | 78% | 63% |
| Severe drainage complications | 63% | 67% |
| Severe complications post-surgery | 65% | 55% |

::: {.callout}
**Trial stopped early** due to excess mortality in PTBD group
:::

---

## ENBD vs EBD Evidence

- Meta-analysis (198 patients):
  - **Cholangitis**: EBD 47.1% vs ENBD 25.5% (OR 0.40, P=.005)
  - **Stent dysfunction**: EBD 62.3% vs ENBD 29.7% (OR 0.26, P<.0001)
- Nagino et al.: ENBD cohort (n=191) → 37% cholangitis, 27% required reintervention

::: {.callout}
**ENBD appears superior in Japanese centers; EBD is at least noninferior to PTBD for resectable pCCA**
:::

---

## When to Avoid Biliary Drainage

- **FLR >50%**: Drainage NOT beneficial
  - Actually associated with **higher** postoperative mortality
  - Farges et al.: Left hemihepatectomy (FLR typically >50%) had lower mortality without preoperative drainage
- **Drain the FLR specifically** — requires expert center to determine resection plan first
- **Contralateral liver** must be drained if focus of cholangitis (e.g., after endoscopic contamination)

---

## Portal Vein Embolization (PVE) {.smaller}

- **Indication**: FLR <40%
- **Goal**: Induce FLR hypertrophy to reduce postoperative liver failure
- First reported by Makuuchi (1990) in 14 pCCA patients — safe, only transient LFT elevations

**Meta-analysis** (Jiao et al., n=1,088 liver resections):

- Morbidity: 2.2%
- Mortality: 0%
- Volume increase: Percutaneous 11.9% vs transileocolic 9.7%

---

## PVE in pCCA: International Study {.smaller}

**1,484 patients** undergoing liver resection for pCCA:

| | Western Centers | Eastern Centers |
|---|-----------------|-----------------|
| PVE use | 7% | 55% (P<.001) |

**Propensity-matched cohort** (n=98):

- Relative volume increase after PVE: **42%** (median 22 days)
- **Liver failure**: 36% → 8% (4.4-fold reduction)
- **Bile leakage**: 35% → 10% (3.5-fold reduction)
- **90-day mortality**: 18% → 7% (2.6-fold reduction)

::: {.callout}
**PVE is safe and recommended for FLR <40%**
:::

---

## ALPPS for pCCA {.smaller}

**Associating Liver Partition and Portal Vein Ligation for Staged Hepatectomy**

- Rapidly induces FLR hypertrophy
- Initially gained popularity after 2007 for select cases

**Outcomes in pCCA**:

- Initial 11 patients: **27% mortality**
- van Gulik et al. (37 patients, 23 centers): **90-day mortality 48%** (14/29)
- Matched analysis: Mortality **twice as high** vs non-ALPPS (P=.100)
- Median OS: 6 months (ALPPS) vs 29 months (controls), P=.048

::: {.callout}
**ALPPS is NOT recommended for pCCA**
:::

---

# Liver Transplantation for pCCA 

## Rationale for Transplantation {.smaller}

- Avoids positive margins (~1/3 of resections)
- Solves inadequate FLR problem
- Treats underlying PSC (if present)

**Mayo Clinic Criteria**:

- Unresectable, confined to liver
- Proximal to cystic duct
- Maximum radial diameter ≤3 cm
- No metastases
- Pretreatment with induction chemoradiation
- Staging surgery with lymph node biopsy to rule out metastases

---
 
## LT Results {.smaller}

| Era | 5-Year Survival |
|-----|-----------------|
| Early LT (no neoadjuvant) | 23% |
| LT + neoadjuvant chemoradiation | **64%** (up to 80% with PSC) |
| Intention-to-treat | 53–56% |

**ILTS Consensus Recommendations**:

- Diagnostic criteria: Dominant stricture + (positive cytology OR FISH polysomy OR CA 19-9 >100 U/mL without cholangitis)
- LT after neoadjuvant chemoradiation in centers with specific protocols
- Prepare for arterial and venous jump grafts

---

## LT vs Resection {.smaller}

- Retrospective comparison:
  - Resection 5-year OS: **18%**
  - LT + neoadjuvant: **64%**
- Subset analysis (R0 resection, no PSC, meeting Mayo criteria):
  - Resection: **29%**
  - LT: **54%** (P=.049)

**TRANSPHIL study**: Ongoing RCT comparing neoadjuvant chemoradiation + LT vs liver resection

::: {.callout}
**Key debate**: Is it selection or induction therapy that drives superior LT outcomes?
:::

---

## Neoadjuvant Therapy for Resection {.smaller}

- Question raised by excellent LT outcomes with neoadjuvant chemoradiation
- **Systematic review**: Only 7 studies, 87 patients total, median accrual period 14 years
- Only 2 studies included upfront resectable patients (n=28 and n=59)
- Protocols varied widely

::: {.callout}
**Insufficient data available** on neoadjuvant (chemo)radiation for resectable pCCA
:::

---

# Prehabilitation

## Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) 

- Multimodal perioperative pathway
- Prehabilitation targets:
  - **Physical** fitness
  - **Nutritional** status
  - **Psychological** health

## Modifiable Risk Factors {.smaller}

- **Albumin <3.5 g/dL** → nutritional optimization
- **Sarcopenia** → exercise and protein supplementation

**Evidence**:

- Exercise prehabilitation improves physical fitness after HPB surgery
- Protein supplementation + home-based exercise → shorter hospital stay (23 vs 30 days, P=.045)
- Effect on complications remains inconclusive

::: {.callout}
**Prehabilitation justified**, especially in patients with modifiable risk factors
:::

---

## Key Takeaways {.smaller}


1. **Refer to expert center BEFORE biliary drainage** — imaging quality is paramount
2. **Left-sided resection preferred** when anatomy allows (larger FLR)
3. **FLR >30–40%** required in pCCA; PVE indicated if <40%
4. **Biliary drainage of FLR** needed if FLR <50%; avoid if FLR >50%
5. **ALPPS is contraindicated** in pCCA (unacceptably high mortality)
6. **LT + neoadjuvant therapy** is viable option for unresectable disease
7. **Prehabilitation** may improve outcomes in modifiable-risk patients
8. **Pathologic confirmation not mandatory** before surgical exploration
